Atomic Structure.a: The number of protons in the nucleus
d: The total mass of the atom
The number of electrons in the outer shell

Atomic Structure.a: Atoms of the same element with different numbers of neutrons
d: Atoms of different elements with the same mass
Atoms with the same number of neutrons but different protons

Where are electrons found in an atom?

The Periodic Table.q: How are elements arranged in the modern periodic table?
The Periodic Table.a: In order of increasing atomic number

The Periodic Table.q: What does the group number tell you about an element?
The Periodic Table.a: The number of electrons in the outer shell

The Periodic Table.q: What does the period number tell you?

The Periodic Table.a: By atomic mass and chemical properties

Groups.q: Why does reactivity increase down Group 1?
Groups.a: The outer electron is further from the nucleus and easier to lose
d: There are more electrons to lose
The atom is larger so it has more mass

Groups.q: Why does reactivity decrease down Group 7?
Groups.a: The outer shell is further from the nucleus and harder to gain an electron
They have a full outer electron shell
d: They are too small to react

Groups.q: What is the correct reactivity order for Group 1 metals?
Groups.a: Potassium more reactive than sodium more reactive than lithium
d: Lithium more reactive than sodium more reactive than potassium

That all atoms have the same structure
